subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should OpenClaw support explicit provider/model overrides for main-session systemEvent cron jobs, and should the public contract be `payload.model`, top-level cron fields, or a `sessionOverride` block?
rationale: Current code treats main-session systemEvent jobs as text-only injections, and enabling overrides crosses provider routing, session state, cron persistence, CLI/UI/docs, and heartbeat execution semantics.

options.title: Design explicit override contract
options.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and require proof that the choice is scoped to one cron run.

options.title: Keep systemEvent text-only
options.body: Document main-session systemEvent jobs as unsupported for model selection and steer cheaper scheduled model calls to isolated/current/custom-session agentTurn jobs.

options.title: Defer to broader cron API work
options.body: Track the decision with broader cron schema and cost-control work so model, context, timeout, fallback, and spend semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Design explicit override contract
recommendation.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and require proof that the choice is scoped to one cron run.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged cron runtime/schema work makes this the strongest available owner for the API and session-state direction decision.
